title: PSMC5 regulates microglial polarization and activation in LPS-induced cognitive deficits and motor impairments by interacting with TLR4.
authors: Bi, Wei; Bao, Keyao; Zhou, Xinqi; Deng, Yihui; Li, Xiaoting; Zhang, Jiawei; Lan, Xin; Zhao, Jiayi; Lu, Daxiang; Xu, Yezi; Cen, Yanmei; Cao, Rui; Xu, Mengyang; Zhong, Wenbin; Zhu, Lihong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PSMC5与TLR4蛋白互作调控小胶质细胞极化，虽用分子动力学模拟验证蛋白-蛋白结合，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Luteolin is a flavonoid found in high concentrations in celery and green pepper, and acts as a neuroprotectant. PSMC5 (proteasome 26S subunit, ATPase 5) protein levels were reduced after luteolin stimulation in activated microglia. We aimed to determine whether regulating PSMC5 expression could inhibit neuroinflammation, and investigate the underlying mechanisms.BV2 microglia were transfected with siRNA PSMC5 before the addition of LPS (lipopolysaccharide, 1.0 microg/ml) for 24 h in serum free DMEM. A mouse model of LPS-induced cognitive and motor impairment was established to evaluate the neuroprotective effects of shRNA PSMC5. Intracerebroventricular administration of shRNA PSMC5 was commenced 7 days prior to i.p. injection of LPS (750 mug/kg). Treatments and behavioral experiments were performed once daily for 7 consecutive days. Behavioral tests and pathological/biochemical assays were performed to evaluate LPS-induced hippocampal damage. Molecular dynamics simulation was used to confirm the interaction between PSMC5 and TLR4 (Toll-like receptor 4) in LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia. SiRNA PSMC5 inhibited BV2 microglial activation, and suppressed the release of inflammatory factors (IL-1beta, COX-2, PGE(2), TNF-alpha, and iNOS) upon after LPS stimulation in BV2 microglia. LPS increased IkappaB-alpha and p65 phosphorylation, which was attenuated by siRNA PSMC5. Behavioral tests and pathological/biochemical assays showed that shRNA PSMC5 attenuated LPS-induced cognitive and motor impairments, and restored synaptic ultrastructure and protein levels in mice. ShRNA PSMC5 reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, PGE(2), and NO) levels in the serum and brain, and relevant protein factors (iNOS and COX-2) in the brain. Furthermore, shRNA PSMC5 upregulated the anti-inflammatory mediators interleukin IL-4 and IL-10 in the serum and brain, and promoted a pro-inflammation-to-anti-inflammation phenotype shift in microglial polarization. Mechanistically, shRNA PSMC5 significantly alleviated LPS-induced TLR4 expression. The polarization of LPS-induced microglial pro-inflammation phenotype was abolished by TLR4 inhibitor and in the TLR-4(-/-) mouse, as in shRNA PSMC5 treatment. PSMC5 interacted with TLR4 via the amino sites Glu284, Met139, Leu127, and Phe283. PSMC5 site mutations attenuated neuroinflammation and reduced pro-inflammatory factors by reducing TLR4-related effects, thereby reducing TLR4-mediated MyD88 (myeloid differentiation factor 88)-dependent activation of NF-kappaB. PSMC5 could be an important therapeutic target for treatment of neurodegenerative diseases involving neuroinflammation-associated cognitive deficits and motor impairments induced by microglial activation.
abstract_zh:
木犀草素是一种在芹菜和青椒中含量较高的类黄酮，具有神经保护作用。在活化的小胶质细胞中，经木犀草素刺激后，PSMC5（蛋白酶体26S亚基，ATP酶5）蛋白水平降低。我们旨在确定调节PSMC5表达是否能抑制神经炎症，并探讨其潜在机制。

在无血清DMEM中，将BV2小胶质细胞转染siRNA PSMC5后，再加入LPS（脂多糖，1.0微克/毫升）处理24小时。建立LPS诱导的认知和运动障碍小鼠模型，以评估shRNA PSMC5的神经保护作用。在腹腔注射LPS（750微克/千克）前7天，开始脑室内给予shRNA PSMC5。治疗和行为实验每天进行一次，连续7天。通过行为测试和病理/生化检测评估LPS诱导的海马损伤。使用分子动力学模拟确认LPS刺激的BV2小胶质细胞中PSMC5与TLR4（Toll样受体4）之间的相互作用。

SiRNA PSMC5抑制了BV2小胶质细胞的活化，并在LPS刺激后抑制了炎症因子（IL-1β、COX-2、PGE(2)、TNF-α和iNOS）的释放。LPS增加了IκB-α和p65的磷酸化，而siRNA PSMC5减弱了这种效应。行为测试和病理/生化检测显示，shRNA PSMC5减轻了LPS诱导的认知和运动障碍，并恢复了小鼠的突触超微结构和蛋白水平。ShRNA PSMC5降低了血清和大脑中促炎细胞因子（TNF-α、IL-1β、PGE(2)和NO）的水平，以及大脑中相关蛋白因子（iNOS和COX-2）的水平。此外，shRNA PSMC5上调了血清和大脑中的抗炎介质白细胞介素IL-4和IL-10，并促进了小胶质细胞极化从促炎表型向抗炎表型的转变。机制上，shRNA PSMC5显著减轻了LPS诱导的TLR4表达。在TLR4抑制剂和TLR-4(-/-)小鼠中，LPS诱导的小胶质细胞促炎表型极化被消除，与shRNA PSMC5处理的效果一致。PSMC5通过氨基酸位点Glu284、Met139、Leu127和Phe283与TLR4相互作用。PSMC5位点突变通过减少TLR4相关效应减轻了神经炎症并降低了促炎因子，从而减少了TLR4介导的MyD88（髓样分化因子88）依赖性NF-κB激活。PSMC5可能成为治疗涉及小胶质细胞活化引起的神经炎症相关认知缺陷和运动障碍的神经退行性疾病的重要治疗靶点。
